Once the smoke flows,

If gathering at the enemy's tunnel,

Thus, the enemy's tunnel assault will be defeated.
When the enemy reaches our city walls,

digging ten feet as before,
stepping down three feet,
and every ten paces, construct horizontal passages on both sides,

for defense.
Bury two jars,
level with the city base,

and cover the planks like a well.
Listen,
one every five paces.
Use compacted materials like pine for tunnel doors,

both extending fully to the door,

Pile stones outside for reinforcement,
seven feet high,
adding battlements on top.
Do not build steps or use stones;
use hanging steps for ascending, descending, and entry/exit.
Prepare furnaces and bellows,
the bellows made of cowhide.
The furnace has two pots,
operated by a bridge mechanism.
For every hundred and ten, use forty for smoking,
then block with burning charcoal,
fill the furnace and cover it,
not allowing gas to escape.
If the enemy quickly approaches within five hundred paces of the tunnel,
and their tunnel's height or depth does not reach ours,

If encountering the enemy in the tunnel,
all should defend and not pursue,

then withdraw and enter the blocked tunnel for defense.
Install a passage,
with a door and lock for it,

Place one dog in each tunnel fortification,
as barking indicates someone's presence.
Cut mugwort into one-foot lengths,
then place them in the kiln furnace,
first building the kiln walls,
connecting them to the tunnel.
Dig wells reaching the city base,
one every three zhang,
based on the external width and narrowness,
ensuring no mistakes.
If the city wall is low and the interior high, follow the interior's difficulty.
Dig wells on the city wall,
making three or four wells,
place new vessels in the wells,
crouch and listen,
carefully determine the tunnel's location,

When the tunnel is nearly encountered,
use a sturdy rod for the counterweighted beam,

and order three strong men to strike with the counterweighted beam,

Quickly dump it into this well,
place mugwort on top,
to seven-tenths full,

and at the bellows' mouth,
pump swiftly.
Use a chariot wheel for covering.
Bundle a load of firewood,

the iron lock three zhang long,
with a ring at one end,
and a hook at the other.
The passage should be seven feet five inches high,
with a foot between pillars,
one pillar every two feet,
pillars set on bases below,
two pillars sharing one round base of eleven.
Two pillars share the same foundation,
with crossbeams and earthen filling.
Pillars should be two and a half arm-spans thick,
firmly set in the earthen filling,
with no pillars intersecting.
Construct two kilns in the tunnel,
both as tunnel shelters,
assign one official and one retainer each,

Block the tunnel entrance,
using two chariot wheels as a screen,

according to the tunnel's height and width,
station people four to five feet inside the tunnel,

When the enemy inside competes to guard the door,
turn and block it.
For a kiln holding three bundles of mugwort,
order the tunnelers to crouch one chi away, guarding one side,

Insert iron spears,
four and a half feet long,
as large as iron armor components,

Place them one chi from the vent,
angled upward,

Install rings and ropes in the tunnel,

Dig wells on the city wall,
wait until the well connects through,
stand on the planks and dig one section,

The counterweighted beam has two arms,
buried firmly with supports on the sides,
and hooks attached to both ends.
Assign fifty workers for tunnel digging,
with men and women in equal numbers.
Fifty men attack the tunnel,

can be lifted and thrown in.
Then, seven men in the tunnel guard the retreat fortifications inside,

To impede the tunnel,
gather wood and tiles from the edge of the城外 moat and scatter them,
fight and cut also in the tunnel,

To hinder approaching tunnels,

metal and support woods four feet long,

When the enemy tunnels,

Make iron hooks and levers,
four feet long, sufficient in quantity,

Make short spears, short halberds, short crossbows, and gadfly arrows,
sufficient in quantity,

Use metal swords for defense,
five feet long.
Make sockets,
wooden stakes,

Prepare to hold jars,

eight feet high,

Use axe metal for chopping,
stakes three feet long,

Build fortifications,

Make adzes, axes, saws, chisels, and picks,

Make iron barriers,

Make medium shields,

four feet wide.
Construct eight horizontal tunnel shields.
Prepare straw and hemp,
sufficient in quantity,

Hold covers,

14.7 "Preparation Against Ant-Rush Attack Sixty-Three"
Qínzǐ bowed repeatedly and said:
May I ask, when the enemy is strong,
and thus escalades the city walls,
those who lag behind are beheaded first,
as a disciplinary measure,
they level the walls as a base,
dig beneath to make chambers,
the front ranks do not stop,
the rear archers shoot swiftly,
what should be done about this?
Mòzǐ said:
Are you asking about defense against ant-rush attacks?
Ant-rush attacks,
are the commander's desperate move,
defend by constructing elevated positions to shoot them,
use mechanisms to impede them,
repel them,
flood them to pressure them,
burn and cover them with bamboo mats,
rain sand and stones on them,
then the ant-rush attack will be defeated.
To defend against ant-rush attacks, make hanging shields,
using wooden boards two inches thick,
three feet front and back,
five feet wide on the sides,
five feet high,
and install them on lower roller carts,
with a turning diameter of one foot six inches.
Have one man wield a square of two zhang,
sharpened at both ends,
positioned inside the hanging shield,
use iron chains to suspend two shields on the upper beam,
install mechanisms,
have four strong men raise and lower them,
without stopping.
Deploy the hanging shields,
generally one every twenty paces,
at the attack points,
one every six paces.
Make accumulations,
bamboo mats one zhang two feet wide and long,
use wood for the upper beam,
bind them with large hemp ropes all over,
soak the ropes in mud,
make iron chains,
hook them to suspend both ends.
If the enemy ant-rushes the city,
burn the mats to cover them,
use connected bamboo sticks and large scoops to rescue.
Use two wheels of a cart,
with a wide space between the axles,
enclose them with a frame,
fix its two ends,
bind the wheels,
cover them all over with mud,
fill inside with elm wood or firewood,
use thorns on the sides,
call it the fire ram,
also called spreading boiling water,
to block the attack path.
If the enemy ascends the path,
burn the spreading boiling water, cut the ropes to drop it,
order brave soldiers to follow and attack them,
have it precede the brave soldiers,
and immediately repair any breaches in the city wall.
Below the city, sufficiently install sharpened stakes,
five feet long,
more than half a large circle in size,
all sharpened at the ends,
arrange in five rows,
with three feet between rows,
buried three feet deep,
planted in a dog-tooth pattern.
Construct the Liánshū,
five chǐ in length,
ten chǐ in width.
The pole is two chǐ long,
six cùn thick,
with a rope two chǐ long.
The hammer
has a handle six chǐ long,
and a head one chǐ five cùn long.
The axe
has a handle six chǐ long,
its blade must be sharp,
all
one placed behind.
The dá is twelve chǐ wide,
◇◇ sixteen chǐ,
hanging front crosspiece four cùn,
both ends overlapping by one chǐ,
do not let them resemble fish scales three,
attach them in the rear row.
Central wooden rope one,
twenty-six chǐ long.
For dá towers that do not meet, block with slips,
frequently dry in the sun,
the dá forms grids,
allowing wind to pass above and below.
For parapets that seem likely to deteriorate,
first bury logs ten chǐ long,
one log per section if damaged, plant firmly,
attach narrow Lǘ Lú boards to the wood,
the Lú boards surface eight chǐ,
seven cùn wide,
one chǐ one cùn in diameter,
repeatedly apply one strike to drive them down,
fix with upper and lower rings and secure them.
One hook in diameter,
wooden tower,
arranged stones.
Hang the dá inside the posts,
not outside the posts.
Blocking grids,
buried four chǐ,
tall ones ten chǐ,
logs of varying lengths mixed,
pointed at the top,
thickly plastered inside and out.
Construct front row gangways,
suspend the dá.
At corners build towers,
towers must curve inward.
Earth,
one every five steps,
not less than twenty piles.
Jué holes,
one every ten chǐ,
three chǐ below the parapet,
wider on the outside.
Turn and patrol the city wall,
towers and scattered items with leather basins,
if the enemy attacks,
soldiers strike from behind,
if neglected and not maintained,
use chariot leather fires.
General method for killing attackers in swarm assaults,
set up barriers outside the city,
ten chǐ from the wall,
barriers ten chǐ thick.
Method for felling barriers,
cut trees of all sizes,
in ten chǐ sections,
separate and bury them deep, tamp firmly,
do not let them be pulled out.
One kill zone every twenty steps,
with a ramp,
ten chǐ thick,
the kill zone has two gates,
gates five steps wide,
barrier gate planks and ladders buried,
do not tamp,
make them easy to pull out.
On the wall, place markers opposite the barrier gates.
Suspend fires,
one stand every four chǐ,
one stove every five steps,
stove gates have furnace charcoal.
Order when all enemies have entered,
chariot fires burn the gates,
suspended fires follow,
deploy carriers and stand ready,
their width matching the file,
one fire between every two carriers,
all stand and wait for the drum signal to ignite,
then launch simultaneously.
If enemies avoid the fire and attack again,
suspended fires descend again,
enemies suffer greatly.
If the enemy retreats and withdraws,
then order our death troops to exit side gates and strike the retreating army,
order elite soldiers and commanders to heed the city drum to exit,
and heed the city drum to re-enter,
according to plan deploy troops and set ambushes,
at midnight drum and shout on all sides of the wall,
enemies will certainly be confused,
breaking their army and killing their generals.
Use white clothes as uniform,
identify by signals.
15.1 "Chapter 68: Rituals for Welcoming the Enemy"
If the enemy comes from the east,
welcome them at the eastern altar,
altar eight chǐ high,
hall depth eight,
eight men aged eighty,
preside over offering to green flags,
eight green deities eight chǐ tall,
eight crossbows,
eight shots then stop,
general's attire must be green,
sacrificial animal a chicken.
If the enemy comes from the south,
welcome them at the southern altar,
altar seven chǐ high,
hall depth seven,
seven men aged seventy,
preside over offering to red flags,
seven red deities seven chǐ tall.
Seven crossbows,
seven shots then stop,
general's attire must be red,
sacrificial animal a dog.
If the enemy comes from the west,
welcome them at the western altar,
altar nine chǐ high,
hall depth nine,
nine men aged ninety,
preside over offering to white flags,
nine white deities nine chǐ tall.
Nine crossbows,
nine shots then stop,
general's attire must be white,
sacrificial animal a goat.
If the enemy comes from the north,
welcome them at the northern altar,
altar six chǐ high,
hall depth six,
six men aged sixty,
preside over offering to black flags.
Six black deities six chǐ tall,
six crossbows,
six shots then stop,
general's attire must be black,
sacrificial animal a pig.
From outer residences to various major shrines,
spiritual shamans may pray there,
provide sacrificial animals.
Generally, observing energies,
there is energy of great generals,
energy of minor generals,
energy of departure,
energy of arrival,
energy of defeat,
those who can clearly discern these,
may know success, failure, fortune, or misfortune.
Promote shamans, doctors, diviners with skills,
store medicines in the palace,
well-prepare quarters.
Energy observation posts near the guard headquarters,
shamans must be near the public altar,
must reverence the spirits.
Shamans and diviners report requests to the commander,
the commander alone knows the requests of shamans and diviners observing energies.
If they spread rumors,
frightening officials and people,
carefully investigate discreetly,
punish without pardon.
Gather worthy officials and those with technical skills or craftsmanship,
assign them ranks.
Promote butchers and brewers,
assign them to kitchens for service,
rank them.
The methods for defending a city are as follows:
The district commander receives his duties,
goes out to inspect the fortifications and follow the moats for defense,
builds shelters and clears the roads,
and repairs the city walls.
All officials contribute resources,
all craftsmen attend to their tasks,
and the minister of war inspects the city walls and organizes the troops.
Guards are posted at the gates,
with two men in charge of the right gate,
two in charge of the left gate,
four in charge of closing them,
and a hundred armored soldiers stationed there.
On the walls, for each step, there is one armored soldier and one halberd,
assisted by three men.
Every five steps has a leader of five,
every ten steps a leader of ten,
every hundred steps a leader of a hundred,
with a senior commander on the flanks,
and a great general in the center,
all having officers and troop leaders.
At the steps on the wall,
officials are stationed to guard them.
Move the central command to a central location,
and report urgent matters promptly.
All soldiers have their duties.
Outside the city,
where arrows reach,
destroy the walls,
so they cannot serve as cover for the enemy.
Within thirty lǐ,
all firewood, reeds, and water are brought inside.
Dogs, pigs, piglets, and chickens are fed their fodder,
their bones collected to make broth,
which revives those with abdominal illnesses.
Inside the city, the firewood, reeds, and huts
where arrows reach
are all covered with shelters.
Order that at dusk, dogs be tied up, horses hobbled, and reins fastened,
and in the quiet night, when drumbeats are heard, shout loudly,
to suppress the enemy's morale,
and to strengthen the resolve of the people,
so that timely shouts prevent the people from falling ill.
The invocators and scribes then make offerings to the four directions, mountains, rivers, and the altars of soil and grain,
before the military actions begin,
and then withdraw.
The lord, in plain attire, makes a vow in the ancestral temple,
saying:
"So-and-so acts without principle,
neglecting righteousness and propriety,
claiming only to be king,
saying:
'I will surely destroy your altars of soil and grain,
and exterminate your people.'
My few loyal followers, strive through the night,
to assist me diligently,
uniting your hearts and combining your strength with all around,
each prepared to die in defense."
After the vow,
the lord withdraws to eat,
lodging to the right of the central ancestral temple,
while the invocators and scribes lodge at the altar of soil.
All officials are fully prepared,
then the battle begins,
with drums beaten at the gate,
flags placed on the right and banners on the left at the corners,
names displayed,
three volleys of arrows shot,
declaring readiness with all five weapons prepared.
Then they descend,
emerge in formation,
and ascend to observe the outskirts.
Orders are given to beat the drums,
and soon they ascend again,
the duty officer shooting from the right of the gate,
with reed arrows,
three volleys of spears,
followed by bows and crossbows,
while inspectors from the left of the gate,
first wave their weapons,
followed by wood and stones.
The invocators, scribes, and ritualists make offerings at the altar of soil,
covering it with a steamer."
15.2 "Flags, Chapter Sixty-Nine"
The methods for defending a city:
wood is represented by a blue flag,
fire by a red flag,
firewood by a yellow flag,
stones by a white flag,
water by a black flag,
food by a mushroom flag,
death-defying warriors by a dark flower flag,
elite soldiers by a rain flag,
numerous troops by a double-hare flag,
men of five feet by a child flag,
women by a shuttle flag,
crossbows by a dog flag,
halberds by a feather grass flag,
swords and shields by a feather flag,
chariots by a mound flag,
cavalry by a bird flag.
For all required items,
if the flag name is not in the book,
use a flag shaped or named after it.
When a flag is raised on the wall,
the official in charge of supplies delivers the goods,
and once sufficient, lowers the flag.
The methods for defending a city require:
accumulation of stones,
accumulation of firewood,
accumulation of reeds and thatch,
accumulation of rushes and reeds,
accumulation of wood,
accumulation of charcoal,
accumulation of sand,
accumulation of pine and cypress,
accumulation of wormwood and mugwort,
accumulation of hemp and fat,
accumulation of metal coins,
accumulation of grain;
wells and stoves have their places,
important hostages have their quarters,
each of the five weapons has its flag,
tallies are distinguishable,
laws and decrees have their upholders,
gradations of severity and reward have their petitions,
and those in charge of road security have their regulations.
Each pavilion captain shall have a banner,
with a pole two zhang five chi long,
and silk cloth one zhang five chi in length,
the width being half a bolt is considered large.
When the enemy approaches and attacks beyond the outer edge of the moat,
beat the drum three times on the wall above the corresponding unit,
and raise one banner.
When they reach the middle of the moat,
beat the drum four times,
and raise two banners.
Upon reaching the palisade,
beat the drum five times,
and raise three banners.
At the auxiliary wall,
beat the drum six times,
and raise four banners.
When they reach the parapet,
beat the drum seven times,
and raise five banners.
Upon reaching the main wall,
beat the drum eight times,
and raise six banners.
If they ascend more than half the height of the main wall,
beat the drum incessantly.
At night, use fires,
following the same counts.
When the enemy retreats and disperses,
reduce the banners accordingly as they advanced,
but without drumming.
The city commander shall have a crimson banner,
fifty chi long.
The generals at the four sides and four gates,
forty chi long.
The next rank,
thirty chi.
Then,
twenty-five chi.
Next,
twenty chi.
After that,
fifteen chi.
The height shall not be less than forty-five chi.
Officials on the wall wear it on their backs,
soldiers on their heads;
officials and soldiers below the wall wear it on their shoulders,
left army on the left shoulder,
right army on the right shoulder,
center army on the chest.
Each has one drum,
the center army one to three.
Each drum is struck three or ten times;
all officials with drums must respond carefully in sequence.
Failing to respond when required,
or responding when not required,
the responsible person shall be beheaded.
Roads are thirty paces wide;
at the stepped paths under the wall, place two wells each,
and set iron jars.
Outside the roads, erect screens,
every thirty paces make an enclosure,
one zhang high.
Build public latrines,
with walls over twelve chi high.
Where alleys meet the main roads,
must have gates,
without a tally,
no passage allowed,
those disobeying the order shall be beheaded.
All officials, soldiers, and civilians in the city shall distinguish themselves by different clothing and insignia,
so men and women can be recognized.
Those defending the barriers,
if they repel the enemy three times,
the commander shall summon them to reward with food in his presence,
grant a large flag,
assign them a hundred-household fief or others' property,
erect the flag at their post,
and make it known to all,
saying it is so-and-so's flag.
Inside the barrier, twenty-five paces wide,
outside, ten paces,
marked according to the terrain.
Train the soldiers in drills,
coordinate front, rear, left, and right,
and rotate those who are tired for rest.
15.3 "Commands Seventy"
The way to secure the state
begins with utilizing the land;
if the land is well utilized, success is achieved;
if not, there is toil without gain.
So it is with people;
those unprepared cannot secure the ruler;
if officials, soldiers, and civilians are of many minds, the responsibility lies with their commanders;
all rewards, punishments, and governance must be based on merit.
The king should frequently send envoys to reward,
bestowing upon those guarding border cities, passes, and preparing against barbarians' toils.
Report on the sufficiency or insufficiency of the commanders' resources,
the terrain that should be defended at the borders,
and where equipment is often abundant.
In border counties and towns:
if the trees are poor,
use less;
if fields are not cultivated,
have less food;
without large buildings or grass roofs,
fewer chariots.
Where wealth is abundant, the people enjoy good food.
Build inner walls,
inner plank roads,
and place equipment on them.
The quarters for officials and soldiers on the wall should all be along the inner roads,
each corresponding to their section,
with two attendants per ten men.
The tally keeper is called the provisioning officer, one person,
responsible for managing the gates.
Gatekeepers and those with guard duties must not allow idlers to linger nearby;
those disobeying shall be executed.
When the enemy arrives,
for a city of a thousand zhang,
must meet them outside the outer wall,
to the advantage of the defenders;
if less than a thousand zhang, do not go out to meet,
but respond according to the enemy's formation and numbers,
this is the essence of city defense.
Matters not covered herein
should be assessed with consideration of both strategy and human affairs.
In defending a city,
the highest priority is to swiftly inflict damage upon the enemy.
Prolonging the defense merely to await reinforcements
demonstrates a lack of understanding of proper defense.
Only by mastering this principle
can one truly defend a city.
The method of city defense:
When the enemy is over a hundred lǐ from the city,
the city commander shall, as ordered, summon all five officials and company leaders,
along with the relatives of wealthy and prominent families,
and house them in government offices,
carefully assigning trustworthy guards to protect them,
ensuring secrecy as the rule.
By the time the enemy approaches the city walls,
the commander’s camp must have no fewer than three hundred soldiers.
For the four sides and four gates,
commanders must be selected from meritorious officials and descendants of those who died in service,
each with a hundred soldiers.
Gate commanders shall also oversee other gates,
with tall towers built flanking each gate,
manned by skilled archers.
The outer wall and secondary ramparts shall each be guarded by one person per section.
Assign the sons of prominent families.
Set up watch posts every fifty steps.
Divide the city into eight districts,
each with an officer,
and each officer accompanied by four subordinates,
to patrol the main roads and neighborhoods.
Elders and minors in the neighborhoods not involved in defense or accounting duties
shall divide the neighborhood into four sections,
each with a head,
to scrutinize those traveling at irregular hours or acting suspiciously,
to uncover conspiracies.
Officers with four or more soldiers under their command
must receive a tally from the general.
When the general sends inspectors on patrol,
they carry the tally;
if the tally does not match or the password is incorrect,
anyone above the rank of squad leader shall detain them
and report to the general.
Failing to detain such persons or allowing subordinates to release them
is punishable by beheading.
For all crimes punishable by death or more,
parents, wives, children, and siblings shall also be implicated.
All men and women defending the city walls
shall be armed sixty percent with crossbows and forty percent with other weapons;
able-bodied women, the elderly, and children
shall each carry a spear.
In case of alarm,
the central army shall rapidly beat the drum three times;
no one may walk on the city walls, roads, or neighborhood streets,
offenders shall be beheaded.
When women join the main army,
order men to walk on the left,
women on the right,
no walking side by side;
all must proceed to their posts.
Disobeying orders is punishable by beheading.
Those who desert their posts shall be publicly executed after three days,
as a measure against treachery.
Neighborhood heads and all others shall guard the neighborhood gates overnight;
when officers patrol their districts,
upon reaching the gate,
the heads shall open it to admit the officers,
and patrol with the elders in charge of defense,
including remote alleys and deserted areas.
Any conspirators plotting treason
shall be executed by chariot-tearing.
If the heads, elders, or officers in charge fail to apprehend them,
all shall be beheaded.
If they succeed,
they are exempted,
and rewarded with two yì of gold per person.
The general shall send inspectors on patrol,
five rounds on long nights,
three on short nights.
Officers on all four sides shall also patrol their own sectors,
following the general’s example;
disobeying orders is punishable by beheading.
All stoves must have screens,
chimneys rising four chǐ above the roof;
take utmost care to avoid fires,
arsonists shall be beheaded;
those causing fires through negligence shall be torn apart by chariots.
If the five-member unit fails to apprehend them,
they shall be beheaded.
If they succeed,
they are exempted.
Firefighters must not make noise;
those who abandon their posts or block alleys to fight fires shall be beheaded.
Heads and elders guarding the alley and district officers
may all assist in firefighting.
District officers must promptly inform the general,
who shall send trusted aides with guards to assist;
officers failing to report shall be beheaded.
Women guilty of capital crimes or fire-related offenses shall not be harmed,
but those using fire for rebellion shall be dealt with according to law.
Critical prohibitions during a siege:
If the enemy suddenly arrives,
strictly order officials and civilians not to clamor, gather in threes, sit weeping, or shed tears.
Gesturing with hands,
pointing,
jostling, stepping on heels,
throwing objects, hitting,
rubbing against others or their clothing,
arguing,
or observing enemy movements without orders
shall be punishable by beheading.
If the five-member unit fails to apprehend them,
they shall be beheaded.
If they succeed,
they are exempted.
If anyone scales the wall to join the enemy,
and the unit fails to stop them,
they shall be beheaded.
If a squad leader defects to the enemy,
the platoon officer shall be beheaded.
If an officer defects,
the platoon commander shall be beheaded.
Defectors’ parents, wives, children, and siblings
shall all be torn apart by chariots.
Those who expose them in advance
are exempted.
When facing the enemy on the main route,
abandoning one’s position
is punishable by beheading.
If the unit fails to apprehend them,
they shall be beheaded.
If they succeed,
they are exempted.
Those who fight fiercely and repel the enemy on the route,
preventing them from ascending again,
shall be rewarded with high stipends for every two soldiers in the unit.
If the siege is overcome,
for a city perimeter of one lǐ or more,
the city commander shall be enfeoffed with thirty lǐ of land as a Guānnèihóu;
the deputy commander shall be awarded the rank of Shàngqīng as ordered;
assistants and officers of equivalent rank shall receive the title of Wǔdàfū;
officials, elites, and those involved in steadfast defense,
ten persons and wall officers equivalent to the five officials,
shall all be granted the rank of Gōngchéng.
Men with defense duties shall receive noble ranks,
two grades each;
women shall be awarded five thousand coins;
men, women, elderly, and children who participated in defense shall receive one thousand coins each,
exempted from corvée for three years,
with no obligations,
and no taxes,
to encourage officials and civilians to hold firm and overcome the siege.
The officers and soldiers stationed at the main gate
shall not exceed two per unit.
The brave shall take the front row,
arranged in squads sitting,
ensuring each knows their left, right, front, and back.
Those who leave their post without authorization,
shall be executed.
The gate captain inspects them three times during the day,
and in the evening,
after the drum signals gate closure, once more.
The commander regularly sends someone to check,
reporting the names of those absent.
Meals are to be taken at the post,
not outside.
The commander must carefully observe the demeanor, expressions, commands, and speech of the receptionists, shield-bearers, attendants, and women serving in front for any irregularities.
All food and drink brought up must be tasted by someone,
and if anything is amiss,
detain and interrogate the reason.
If the commander is displeased with any receptionist, shield-bearer, attendant, or woman serving in front,
he may order them beheaded, assaulted, or bound.
Those who disobey orders or delay in binding shall be executed.
They must be routinely warned.
All those standing or sitting at the gate morning and evening
shall be ordered by age from young to old,
taking their positions at dawn and dusk.
Priority is given to those with merit and ability,
the rest stand in order.
Every five days,
officials shall report one instance of frivolity, improper conduct, or bullying.
When external envoys or visitors arrive,
they must have credentials,
which are returned upon departure.
If touring the county,
send a trusted person to first notify the residence,
then meet at the gate,
after which the commander enters the quarters.
Subordinates should constantly observe their superiors,
following them;
when superiors ascend, do not follow down,
but must ◇◇ follow.
Guest soldiers guarding the host,
and those acting as guards,
the host also guards the guest soldiers.
For garrison soldiers in the city,
if their hometown is under enemy attack,
be vigilant,
frequently checking their posts.
Those from the same locality
must not guard together.
Issue tallies to gate officers;
if the tally matches, allow entry and reward;
if not,
detain,
and report to the commander.
Those ascending the wall
with improper clothing or other violations
shall have the night drum placed at the commander's main gate.
At dusk,
order cavalry or envoys holding tokens closing the city to all carry warrants.
At evening drum,
after ten beats,
all gate towers are closed.
Those walking about shall be executed,
but first interrogate the reason for movement,
then carry out the punishment.
At dawn appearance,
the officer in charge beats the drum,
permitting movement.
Gate officers each enter,
request keys to open the gates,
and return the keys immediately after.
Those with tallies or tokens
are exempt from this order.
When the enemy arrives,
beat the tower drum five times,
followed by surrounding drums,
and mixed small drums respond.
After five small drum beats, those joining the army,
execute if tardy.
Orders must be sufficiently fearsome,
rewards sufficiently beneficial,
commands must be enforced.
Upon issuing orders, assign people to follow up,
checking what is implemented or not.
Passwords:
evening has a password,
missing the password,
execution.
Establish defense regulations and label them as such,
posting them at streets, intersections, steps, or gates,
so passersby can see and comply.
Any officer, soldier, or civilian plotting to kill or injure their superior
is guilty of treason.
Those who capture or report such,
reward with twenty catties of gold,
pardoning their crimes.
Taking what is not within one's duty without authorization,
or handling matters not under one's jurisdiction,
execution.
Any officer, soldier, or civilian entering another's sector without permission
shall be arrested
and handed over to the Director of Construction or the scout;
the scout reports to the commander.
Not arresting but releasing without authority,
execution.
Anyone capturing a rebel, city traitor, wall climber, or defector
can, by order, exempt two persons from death penalty,
or four from hard labor.
Those who betray the city or abandon their parents to flee,
along with their parents, wives, and children
—record all civilian building timber and stones like defensive stones in quantity,
noting lengths and sizes.
Failure to report as required,
the officer is guilty.
All officers, soldiers, and civilians on the wall
shall guarantee their neighbors;
if neighbors commit crimes unknown to them,
their squad is guilty.
If they personally capture criminals or report to officers,
both are rewarded.
If not in the same squad but aware of another squad's crime,
double the reward.
Families in the city's lower wards also guarantee left, right, front, and back,
as on the wall.
If the city is small and crowded,
relocate the elderly, weak, and those from other states to larger cities.
When the enemy arrives,
assessing inevitable attack,
the defenders first clear the areas outside the walls,
but do not burn them.
With the enemy below the walls,
rotate officer and soldier posts periodically,
but not the support staff,
who are not allowed on the wall.
With the enemy below,
gather all pots and jars,
piling them beneath the walls,
one pile every hundred paces,
five hundred in total.
No rooms inside the gate;
build a surrounding office,
with a pillar four chi high,
as a lookout.
Install inner gates on the ramparts,
two gates per battlement.
Clear the area outside the city walls,
within a hundred paces of the moat,
demolishing all walls, fences, and trees large and small.
Where the enemy approaches,
such as hidden paths, nearby areas, or city grounds,
erect watchtowers,
planting bamboo spikes in the open.
Build a large tower below the commander's hall,
overlooking the city,
with surrounding passages below,
for receiving guests,
who wait to be seen.
Occasionally summon the three elders and officials from the left protection zone to discuss plans, prioritizing
virtuous conduct,
and if strategies align,
they enter the protected area.
Once in protection,
do not walk the walls,
do not leave the quarters.
All defenders must know the low walls and shallow moats and guard accordingly.
Use morning and evening soldier songs as a measure,
employing fewer people for easier defense.
Outside the city, the magistrate is responsible;
inside, the commander.
If the magistrate, deputy, or captain
flees,
capture counts as replacement;
if over ten people,
the magistrate, deputy, and captain each lose two ranks;
if over a hundred,
they are dismissed
and serve as soldiers.
Those seeking replacements
must capture enemy prisoners to be considered.
Recruit people who wish to trade goods, grain, or millet for any kind of utensils,
and ultimately sell them at market price.
If fellow townspeople, acquaintances, or brothers commit crimes,
even if not within the county but wish to redeem them,
using grain, millet, money, gold, cloth, silk, or other valuables to secure their release,
order that it be permitted.
Assign one messenger every ten paces,
and those who delay messages or fail to transmit them,
shall be executed.
For all matters that can facilitate affairs,
urgently report them in writing to the commander.
If officials, soldiers, or civilians wish to report matters,
urgently convey their messages,
and request them from the officials.
Those who delay or fail to report various matters,
shall be executed.
Each county shall report the number of its local heroes, strategists, resident nobles, and influential households.
Government offices, city walls, and all officials, soldiers, and civilians
shall guard against fires in mutual protection from all directions.
If a fire breaks out and spreads,
and the flames蔓延 and burn people,
the responsible shall be executed.
All who use strength in numbers to bully the weak or fewer, or forcibly violate women,
or cause clamor,
shall be executed.
At all city gates or watchtowers,
carefully inspect the tallies of travelers coming and going.
If tallies are suspicious or lacking,
all shall go to the county court to report and request,
and be questioned about their mission.
Those with proper tallies
shall be well accommodated in government offices.
If their acquaintances or brothers wish to see them,
summon them,
but do not allow them to enter the inner alleys.
The village elders guarding the lanes shall order the repair officers to administer floggings.
If others with minor matters are not allowed into the villages,
the village elders shall not enter private homes.
Transmit orders within the villages using feathers,
with feathers placed at three different locations.
Each household shall order its members to their posts.
Those who fail to obey orders or delay them,
shall be executed.
Households with guards shall manage food.
If officials, soldiers, or civilians enter lanes and alleys without tallies,
and the government officials or village elders guarding the lanes fail to strictly stop them,
all shall be executed.
All who steal guarded equipment, property, or steal from each other,
worth one coin or more,
shall be executed.
Officials, soldiers, and civilians shall each write their names largely on tablets,
displaying them at their posts.
The commander inspects their posts,
and those who enter without authorization shall be executed.
On the city walls, distribute mats and bedding once daily,
ensuring they are交错 distributed.
Those who conceal and not report others carrying hidden prohibited items,
shall be executed.
When officials, soldiers, or civilians die,
immediately summon their families and the secondary minister of works to bury them,
not allowing them to sit and weep.
Those severely injured shall be sent home for treatment,
with their families caring well for them,
providing doctors and medicine,
granting two shēng of wine daily,
two jīn of meat,
and ordering officials to frequently inspect the lanes,
observing if the sick have recovered,
then promptly reporting for duty.
Those who fake self-inflicted injuries to evade duties,
shall be executed with their families.
After matters are settled,
the commander shall send officials personally to the homes of the dead and injured,
visiting the households to mourn sorrowfully.
When the enemy retreats and affairs conclude,
conduct sacrificial prayers.
The commander shall order to reward local heroes who fought bravely and all who achieved merits,
personally visiting the homes of the dead and injured to mourn them,
and personally meet the descendants of those who died in service.
When the city siege ends,
the ruler shall urgently send envoys to offer慰劳,
enumerating the meritorious and the count of dead and injured,
bestowing ranks and emoluments,
with the commander personally honoring and favoring them,
clearly valuing them,
to make their resentment focus on the enemy.
Soldiers or officials on the city walls shall each guard their left and right,
and if anyone seeks to conspire with the outside against the city,
their parents, wives, children, and siblings shall all be executed.
If those on the left or right know of it
but do not capture or report it,
all shall share the same crime.
Households in the city's lower villages shall mutually protect each other,
as per the regulations on the city walls.
Those able to capture or report such conspirators
shall be enfeoffed with a thousand-household邑.
If those not from their left or right but from other squads capture or report,
they shall be enfeoffed with a two-thousand-household邑.
City prohibitions:
Making soldiers or civilians unwilling to resist the enemy, feign duties, or harmonize banners,
shall be executed.
Those not obeying orders,
shall be executed.
Those issuing orders without authorization,
shall be executed.
Those failing to follow orders,
shall be executed.
Leaning on halberds or descending the city walls,
and not aligning with the ranks,
shall be executed.
Shouting wildly without cause,
shall be executed.
Those losing their equipment,
shall be executed.
Praising the enemy or slandering internally,
shall be executed.
Leaving posts to gather and talk,
shall be executed.
Hearing the city drum signals to assemble,
and reporting late to posts,
shall be executed.
Each person shall write their name largely on a board,
placing it at their post's partition.
The commander must personally plan their rotations,
and those entering unauthorized posts without reason,
shall be executed.
Leaving posts with left or right companions to enter other posts,
and the companions not capturing them,
carrying private letters,
conducting personal visits,
or delivering messages,
neglecting guard duties for private matters,
soldiers or civilians stealing from each other—
all, including families and infants, shall be executed without pardon.
Report and record them.
Those without tallies横行 in the army,
shall be executed.
When the enemy is at the city walls,
frequently change their assignments but not their provisions.
Praising the enemy's few as many,
chaos as order,
or clumsy attacks as skillful,
shall be executed.
Enemy and host must not converse or interact,
the enemy shooting messages,
must not be praised,
external displays of goodwill internally,
must not be responded to,
all not obeying orders shall be executed.
Prohibit raising arrow messages or shooting letters to the enemy,
violators of the order,
their parents, wives, and children shall all be executed,
and their bodies displayed on the city walls.
Those able to capture or report such offenders,
shall be rewarded with twenty jīn of gold.
Those moving at unauthorized times,
only the commander and those holding the governor's tally as envoys are allowed.
When the commander enters to oversee the city,
must carefully inquire among elders and officials about any unresolved grudges or enmities,
summon the involved,
and clearly mediate for them.
The commander must personally distinguish such individuals and record them,
isolating them.
Those using personal grudges to harm the city or official matters,
their parents, wives, and children shall all be executed.
Those conspiring with the outside against the city,
shall have their three clans executed.
Those able to capture or report such conspirators,
shall be enfeoffed according to the size of the defended邑,
the commander returning to confer the seal,
honoring and appointing them to office,
making officials, soldiers, and civilians all clearly aware.
For heroes with many external connections to feudal lords, frequently summon them,
ensure the superiors are informed,
treat them well and keep them close,
the local officials shall repeatedly select and provide for them,
not allowing them to enter or exit without authorization.
Use the method of linked hostages,
for village elders, parents, and the relatives, parents, wives, and children of heroes,
must honor and favor them.
If poor people cannot feed themselves,
the authorities shall provide food.
For the parents, relatives, wives, and children of brave warriors,
regularly bestow wine and meat,
must respect them,
and house them near the governor.
The guard tower facing the hostage palace must be well-enclosed,
with its walls densely plastered,
so that those below cannot see above,
while those above can see below,
preventing those underneath from knowing whether there are people above or not.
Those appointed by the commander should be upright, incorruptible, loyal, trustworthy, and harmless individuals capable of handling affairs.
Do not restrict their consumption of food and wine;
money, gold, cloth, silk, and other valuables should be kept by each themselves,
taking care not to steal from one another.
The walls of the hostage palace must be triple-layered,
and on the parapets,
the guards should pile pottery shards.
There should be officials at the gates,
with the person in charge inside the gate,
and the keys must be controlled with the governor's seal.
For protection, select seasoned garrison soldiers of稳重 character.
Choose officials who are loyal, trustworthy, harmless, and capable of handling duties.
Order the guards to build a ten-foot wall themselves,
encircling the perimeter.
As for the gates and side doors,
do not allow the guards to control the main gate.
The residence of the astrologers must be near the governor,
and the shamans' quarters near the public shrine,
showing respect to the spirits.
Shamans, priests, and historians, along with astrologers, must report good news to the people,
and request to inform the governor,
with only the governor knowing their petitions.
Do not allow astrologers to spread false, alarming rumors among the people—
punish without pardon.
If food is insufficient,
order the people to report the amount of grain in their households in shēng,
setting a deadline,
with those in charge of records
officials verifying together.
Those who fail to report by the deadline or
report incompletely,
if discovered by officers,
shall all be punished.
Those who capture or report offenders
shall receive a thirty percent reward.
Collect grains, cloth, silk, money, gold, and livestock,
all at fair prices,
issuing receipts to the owners,
recording it,
and after the matter,
repaying them double the value.
Also, grant titles based on the value and quantity of their contributions.
Those wishing to become officials may do so;
those preferring rewards, titles, or salaries instead,
or to redeem relatives or acquaintances who are criminals,
may do so as permitted by order.
Those receiving rewards
should be presented at the hostage palace,
to be with their families.
Those wishing to further assist the authorities
shall have their titles and rewards doubled.
For example, a certain son from a certain village with two mouths to feed,
has stored 600 dàn of grain;
another from a different village with ten mouths,
has 100 dàn.
Set deadlines for grain distribution;
those failing to comply shall have it confiscated by the nobility.
Those who obtain or
report such cases
shall receive a thirty percent reward.
Take care to keep the people unaware of our grain reserves.
Upon entering the city, the commander should start with scouts,
immediately housing and providing for them upon acquisition,
without revealing our defense preparations.
Scouts should have separate quarters,
with their parents, wives, and children housed together,
granted clothing, food, and wine,
and treated well by trusted officials.
When scouts return or report,
meet them privately.
The commander's residence should have three layers of defense,
with outer corner towers,
inner towers,
and covered pathways extending 1.5 zhàng into the hostage palace.
The hostages shall not have private rooms;
mats and bedding are issued every three days,
with brief inspections.
Spread straw in the palace,
over three chǐ thick.
Dispatch scouts from loyal, trustworthy, and respected local families,
with relatives, wives, and children,
generously supported.
Send scouts in rotations,
providing for their parents and families,
in separate quarters,
not mixed with others,
supplying food and wine.
Send additional scouts,
supporting them like the previous ones.
Upon return,
cross-examine their reports;
if verified,
reward them generously.
Scouts sent three times and verified thrice
receive double rewards;
those preferring official positions over rewards
may be appointed as 200 dàn officials,
with the commander personally granting the seal.
Those preferring rewards and salaries over office
shall be treated as before.
Those penetrating deep into enemy territory,
if their intelligence is accurate,
receive double the reward of other scouts;
those preferring office over reward
may be appointed as 300 dàn officials.
For defenders receiving rewards,
the commander must personally deliver them to their families,
demonstrating the commander's commitment.
Those wishing to further assist the authorities
shall have rewards, titles, salaries, or redemption of criminals doubled.
Scouts should not go beyond ten lǐ.
Erect markers on high, convenient grounds,
with three guards per marker,
and three markers leading to the city,
visible to beacon fires on the walls—
raising smoke by day,
fire by night.
Upon learning the enemy's approach
and confirming an attack,
if small cities cannot defend their access,
evacuate all elderly, weak, grain, and livestock.
Dispatch no more than fifty scouts;
when the enemy reaches the ramparts,
withdraw them,
avoiding complacency.
Scout groups should not exceed three hundred,
sent out at dusk
for covert duties.
Block empty paths and strategic points,
where people pass,
make them detectable,
with at least three trackers per village,
patrolling level grounds.
Each sets up markers,
answered by the city walls.
When scouts move beyond the outer markers,
post guards outside the outer gate,
set markers inside,
and station half the troops inside the gate,
keeping their numbers undisclosed.
In case of alarm,
if the enemy crosses the outer markers,
the wall signals with flags,
guards beat drums,
and prepare for battle as directed.
Upon sighting the enemy, raise one banner;
upon entering the border, two;
approaching the outer walls, three;
entering the outer walls, four;
approaching the city, five.
At night, use fire signals similarly.
Within a hundred steps of the outer walls,
clear all walls, trees large and small;
seal external wells,
preventing water drawing;
demolish external buildings,
and cut down all trees.
Gather all potential siege tools inside the city,
with each person marking their items.
After the event,
retrieve them by their marks.
Officials issue vouchers,
recording the counts.
If lumber cannot all be brought in,
burn it,
denying the enemy its use.
Have individuals write on large boards
and display them at their posts to show loyalty.
When officials present their governance,
those who follow licentious laws,
their crime is punishable by arrow shooting.
Those obsessed with appearances and deceitful speech,
disorderly and unruly,
blocking the road and hindering the masses,
abandoning duties and procrastinating,
failing to maintain peace over time,
their crime is punishable by arrow shooting.
Creating uproar and alarming the masses,
their crime is punishable by death.
Those who do not remonstrate with superiors,
or spread ominous words to secondary leaders,
their crime is punishable by death.
No one dares to possess musical instruments or worn-out steeds in the army;
if found, the crime is punishable by arrow shooting.
Without orders from the officials,
no one dares to have chariots galloping or people rushing;
if found, the crime is punishable by arrow shooting.
No one dares to let cattle and horses roam freely in the army;
if found, the crime is punishable by arrow shooting.
Eating and drinking at improper times,
their crime is punishable by arrow shooting.
No one dares to sing or wail in the army;
if found, the crime is punishable by arrow shooting.
Order each to enforce penalties and execute fully;
if officials see crimes but do not punish,
they share the penalty;
if anyone escapes,
they are also executed.
Any commander who leads his troops into battle unlawfully,
is executed.
If officials do not ensure that soldiers, clerks, and civilians hear the oath and orders,
they bear the punishment instead.
All executions are carried out in the market,
displaying the dead to public view.
Heralds await orders outside the gate,
seated in two rows flanking the entrance,
taking turns eating,
leaving no post empty.
One elder among the gate heralds,
guards repeatedly order inspections inside to find those missing,
supervising the gate captain and their officers,
and report missing persons inside.
Four men sit flanking the order gate inside,
two sit flanking the side gate outside,
when visitors appear,
they hold weapons and stand forward,
taking turns eating,
recording the names of those on duty.
Those in high towers guarding the residence,
upon seeing carriages or cavalry approaching from outside the road,
or unusual activity in the city,
immediately report to the commander.
The commander verifies with reports from city watchtowers, gate guards, and local officials.
Those below the tower receive the watchers' words,
and report to the commander.
Two palace attendants,
sit flanking the side gate inside,
the gate always closed,
taking turns eating.
One elder among the palace attendants.
Around the pathways of the guarded palace,
set up stationed routes,
each with walls on both sides,
ten feet high,
forming parapets.
Erect initial chicken-foot placements.
Flanking and overseeing provisions.
If intercepted documents are obtained,
must carefully examine and cross-verify,
if unlawful,
stop and interrogate.
Stationed formations and walls outside pathways and streets all have towers,
overlooking the neighborhoods,
each tower has one drum and a stove.
If an incident occurs,
beat the drum,
stop when officials arrive,
at night use fire to point to the drum's location.
One latrine every fifty paces below the city,
latrines and above share the same sewer.
Those with offenses that need not be severely punished,
order them to clean latrines as benefit.
15.4 "Miscellaneous Defense Seventy-One"
Qínzǐ asked:
The enemy is numerous and brave,
lightly showing their might,
to intimidate the defenders,
bringing up firewood and soil together,
building ramps like sheep pens,
piling earth high,
to overlook our people,
advancing with shields covered,
connecting to the city walls,
ascending with weapons and crossbows,
what can be done about this?
Mòzǐ said:
You ask about defending against ramps?
Ramps are
a clumsy method of attack,
sufficient to weary soldiers,
but insufficient to harm the city.
Against ramp tactics,
distant attacks cause distant harm,
near the city causes near harm,
but not reaching the city.
Arrows and stones never cease,
left and right swiftly shoot,
with barriers as rear support,
secured by watchtowers.
Sharpen our elite troops,
carefully prevent them from looking back,
defenders hold firm below,
attackers lightly retreat.
Cultivate courage and high morale,
the people's spirit hundredfold,
capture many and reward frequently,
then soldiers will not be weary.
If earthworks continue unabated,
unable to stop the assault,
and they connect to the city,
respond with methods against cloud ladders.
All methods to counter tunnels, rams, cloud ladders, and overlooks,
must involve widening the city for defense.
If time is insufficient,
then use wood to encase it,
left a hundred paces,
right a hundred paces.
Shower down arrows, stones, sand, and lime like rain,
aid with firewood, fire, and boiling water.
Select and sharpen elite troops,
carefully prevent them from looking back,
judiciously reward and enforce penalties,
keeping calm as the principle,
follow with urgency,
prevent arising concerns,
nurture courage and high fervor,
the people's spirit hundredfold,
capture many and reward frequently,
then soldiers will not slacken.
Rams, overlooks, and ladders are all countered with rams.
Channels are fifteen feet long,
buried three feet,
posts twelve feet long.
Channels sixteen feet wide,
their base twelve feet,
hanging part four feet,
set channels without attaching leaves five inches.
One ladder channel every ten zhang.
Ladder channels and shields in general,
two hundred fifty-eight channels per li,
one hundred twenty-nine shields.
Various external roads that can be fortified to hinder enemies,
the most critical points build three watchtowers,
each tower triangular,
arranged like the Weaving Maiden,
enabling mutual rescue.
All distant hills, forests, ditches, mounds, fields, outer gates, or alleyways,
can be fortified,
and set with hidden markers,
to trace the number of comings and goings and hiding places.
Protect the people,
first arrange city offices, residences, and buildings,
large and small coordinated.
Those protected wishing to join brothers or acquaintances,
permit it.
External grain, livestock, wealth, and goods that can aid the city,
send into the city;
if urgent,
then pile inside the gates.
Sentinels no more than fifty,
enemies arrive, follow leaves to retreat,
only cover if caught.
People offering grain, cloth, money, cattle, or livestock,
all set at fair price,
issuing vouchers to owners.
Enable each to use their strengths,
and all under heaven's affairs align;
balance their duties,
and all under heaven's affairs succeed;
if all are content,
all under heaven's affairs are prepared;
strengths and weaknesses have measures,
and all under heaven's affairs are complete.
When building postal relay stations, make them circular,
over three zhàng high,
and order them to construct slanted ladders.
The ladder has two arms,
each three chǐ long,
with a three-chǐ gap at the entrance,
fastened together with ropes.
Use layered planks
to make suspension bridges.
Install chimneys,
with one drum per station.
For enemy beacon fires, alert beacon fires, and chaotic beacon fires,
transmit the fire signals in sequence,
stopping only when reaching the capital.
In urgent situations,
raise and lower them repeatedly.
Once the beacon fire is raised,
immediately transmit it with five drumbeats,
and also use fire to indicate
the direction from which the enemy is coming and their approximate numbers,
reporting back by morning.
If the enemy comes and goes intermittently,
do not cease the beacon fires.
Upon sighting the enemy,
raise one beacon fire;
when they enter the territory,
raise two beacon fires;
when they attack the outskirts,
raise three beacon fires and beat one drum;
when they assemble outside the outer wall,
raise four beacon fires and beat two drums;
when they gather at the city walls,
raise five beacon fires and beat five drums.
At night, use fire signals
in the same quantities.
Those guarding the beacon fires must act urgently.
Dispatch them at dusk,
ordering all to perform their duties diligently.
Ensure that hills, forests, and other terrain can be tracked;
begin tracking at dawn,
with no fewer than three trackers per lǐ,
each standing at their markers,
and the city wall responding accordingly.
Sentinels set up field markers when going out,
stationed inside and outside the outer wall,
erecting flags and banners.
Half the troops remain inside,
making their numbers unpredictable.
In case of alarm,
raise the empty marker;
upon seeing the enemy,
raise the pastoral marker.
The city wall directs with flags,
sentinels advance with drumbeats,
arranging flags and banners for battle,
following the direction of the flags.
Men in the fields prepare for battle alongside the sentinels,
while women quickly retreat inside.
Once the enemy is spotted,
drum signals transmit until they reach the city.
Three guards are stationed at the markers,
taking turns to watch from raised markers.
The commander frequently orders cavalry or officials to patrol and observe,
ensuring awareness of all activities.
Their unit beats one drum;
upon sighting the enemy,
they beat drums,
transmitting until the city is reached.
For one dǒu of food,
the annual total is thirty-six shí.
For two-thirds consumption,
the annual total is twenty-four shí.
For half consumption,
the annual total is eighteen shí.
For two-fifths consumption,
the annual total is fourteen shí and four dǒu.
For one-third consumption,
the annual total is twelve shí.
One shēng meal provides five shēng,
two-thirds meal provides three and a small half shēng,
half meal provides two and a half shēng,
two-fifths meal provides two shēng,
one-third meal provides one and a large half shēng,
with two meals per day.
In times of famine relief,
two shēng per day for twenty days,
three shēng per day for thirty days,
four shēng per day for forty days,
thus sparing the people from ninety days of deprivation.
When the enemy is near,
urgently collect all miscellaneous household utensils, bronze, iron, and anything else that can aid defense.
First list the government buildings and non-essential offices,
noting the size, length, and quantity of materials,
and dispatch them urgently as needed.
When the enemy approaches,
demolish houses and cut down trees;
even if there are pleas,
do not heed them.
Do not stack firewood in fish-scale patterns;
align it with the pathways,
making it easy to retrieve.
For timber that cannot all be brought in,
burn it,
preventing the enemy from using it.
Stack wood
according to length, size, and quality,
with each side of the city storing it internally,
and larger logs fitted with rings
before being piled up.
For city defenders of司马Sīmǎ rank and above,
their parents, siblings, wives, and children must be held as hostages in the headquarters
to ensure steadfast defense.
Appoint a Dū Sīkōng,
with four in large cities,
and two sentinels.
County sentinels
are one per side.
Tíng Wèi and deputy Sīkōng
are one per station.
Officials serving at the command post
must be financially sufficient, honest, and trustworthy,
with parents, siblings, wives, and children in the Bǎogōng
to qualify as attendant officials.
All officials must have hostages
to be assigned duties.
Two guards are stationed at the main gate,
standing on either side,
ordering passersby to hurry outside.
Each has four jǐ,
standing by the gate,
with personnel sitting beneath them;
officials inspect them five times daily,
reporting the names of those who flee.
Outside the moat, at key and hazardous points,
set up decoy figures,
ordering night patrols to shoot at them,
targeting the sparse areas.
In the water outside the walls, place bamboo arrows,
with arrow fields two steps wide,
arrows five cùn below the water surface,
mixed in length,
arranged in three rows at the outer edge,
facing outward,
and inward rows facing inward.
Every thirty steps, set up a crossbow shelter,
ten chǐ wide,
and one zhàng two chǐ long.
Every hundred steps, form a squad;
if a squad is in emergency,
dispatch the nearest for support urgently,
with the next squad taking over their position.
For defense tallies,
used for entry and exit missions,
the tally master must record in detail,
noting the circumstances,
specifying the nature of the task,
and awaiting their return report for verification.
When a tally is issued,
the gate from which the envoy departs
must state the time of issuance and the bearer's name.
Corridors connect to the commander's quarters,
interweaving through rooms.
Build elevated pathways,
constructing walls,
with the walls well-fortified on top.
Gather provisions,
ordering households to store three years' worth of vegetables and grains,
to prepare for floods and droughts,
as years are not always normal.
Order border counties to preemptively plant and store wūhuì, yún, wūhuì, and zhūyè,
and fill in ditches and wells in outer residences if possible,
or if not,
place these plants there.
In peace, show the appearance of danger;
in danger, show the appearance of peace.
When the enemy arrives,
order all doors and windows to be chiseled with holes of two types,
each in two categories,
one chiseled to attach ropes,
with ropes four chǐ long,
as thick as a finger.
When the enemy arrives,
first slaughter the cattle, sheep, chickens, dogs, ducks, geese, and pigs,
all skinned,
collect their hides, sinews, horns, fat, bristles, and feathers.
Officials prepare catalpa and paulownia wood,
make iron tips,
use thick bamboo for crossbeams and pillars,
if the situation is urgent and cannot be handled remotely,
order the digging up of trees from the outer estate's woods,
assess the quantity,
and if fortifying the city for defense,
make it triangular,
weighing over five catties.
Soak all timber in water,
not exceeding one raft's worth.
Coat thatched roofs or piled firewood,
with a thickness of over five inches.
Officials shall each report the resources within their jurisdiction that can aid in defense,
and submit them.
There are slanderers,
benefactors,
evil people,
good people,
tall people,
strategists,
brave warriors,
skilled artisans,
envoys,
those who are insiders,
outsiders,
those who are virtuous,
and those with virtuous followers.
The commander must investigate the reasons for their actions,
and only admit them after verifying their claims.
If the people dislike or criticize officials,
the explanations given by officials
should all be recorded in writing and stored,
to await reports for cross-reference.
Those who are short, under five chi, and unfit for military service,
assign them as minor officials,
ordering them to serve in government offices or residences.
Boulders for defense and sharp arrows,
all materials and utensils must be carefully organized,
each with allocated quantities.
Prepare carts for transporting supplies to the city walls,
using light carriages,
with sturdy wheels,
ten chi wide,
shafts one zhang long,
with three spokes,
six chi in width.
Make wooden boxes,
as long as the shafts,
four chi high,
well-covered on top,
and arranged inside to carry arrows.
Mòzǐ said:
There are five reasons a city cannot be defended.
The city is large but the people are few—
the first reason it cannot be defended.
The city is small but the population is dense—
the second reason it cannot be defended.
The people are many but food is scarce—
the third reason it cannot be defended.
The market is far from the city—
the fourth reason it cannot be defended.
Supplies are stored outside,
and the wealthy reside in remote areas—
the fifth reason it cannot be defended.
A rule of thumb: ten thousand households for a city of three li square.
